title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #16

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why should you underline new words in a text? (1 mark)
   A. To count pages
   B. So you can find their meanings and learn them
   C. To hide them
   D. To spoil the book

2. What does legible writing mean? (1 mark)
   A. Writing very small
   B. Writing in capital letters only
   C. Writing with a red pen
   D. Writing that can be read easily

3. What does an oral text mean? (1 mark)
   A. A text that is spoken
   B. A text drawn on paper
   C. A text written on a wall
   D. A text printed only

4. Which sentence should be read with a rising voice in English? (1 mark)
   A. Are you coming to school?
   B. We go to school.
   C. You are coming to school.
   D. Come to school.

5. Which habit helps you listen well? (1 mark)
   A. Talking to a neighbour
   B. Playing with a pencil
   C. Looking at the floor
   D. Sitting where you can see and hear the speaker

6. Which question word asks about a person? (1 mark)
   A. Where
   B. When
   C. Who
   D. How many

7. In the story of Otieno, what caused his burn? (1 mark)
   A. He played with a dog
   B. He touched the handle of the hot pot
   C. He ate hot food
   D. He fell from a tree

8. How are words arranged in a dictionary? (1 mark)
   A. By size of the word
   B. By colour
   C. By the number of letters
   D. In alphabetical order

9. What is the best way to read your part in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Read other people's lines
   B. Read it very quickly
   C. Practise your lines with the right feeling
   D. Never practise

10. Which word shows the first step? (1 mark)
   A. Finally
   B. First
   C. In the end
   D. Lastly

11. Which sentence is a metaphor? (1 mark)
   A. The classroom was busy.
   B. The classroom was as busy as a beehive.
   C. The classroom was a beehive.
   D. The classroom was like a beehive.

12. What should you do when you use a simile or metaphor? (1 mark)
   A. Use very many in one sentence
   B. Never explain it
   C. Choose a comparison your listeners will understand
   D. Use hurtful comparisons

13. What is a reading club? (1 mark)
   A. A group that sells books
   B. A team for running
   C. A choir
   D. A group that meets to share and discuss books

14. Why do many readers read silently? (1 mark)
   A. It is boring
   B. It is illegal to read aloud
   C. It is fast and does not disturb others
   D. Books cannot be read aloud

15. What does Many hands make light work mean? (1 mark)
   A. Hands are light
   B. Nobody should help
   C. Work is always easy
   D. Work is easier when people share it

16. Which is a character in a story? (1 mark)
   A. A girl called Neema
   B. The rainy season
   C. The end
   D. A shady tree

17. A good ending to an imaginative story usually (1 mark)
   A. starts a new problem always
   B. solves the problem or shows the lesson
   C. has no full stops
   D. repeats the title

18. Which is a proverb? (1 mark)
   A. Please sit down
   B. A stitch in time saves nine
   C. It is Monday
   D. Bring your book

19. What kind of word is when in When I arrived, the shop was closed? (1 mark)
   A. A noun
   B. A conjunction
   C. A number
   D. An adjective

20. What is a personal experience? (1 mark)
   A. A story from a book
   B. A rule
   C. Something that happened to you
   D. A number

21. Which of these should you include when describing an event? (1 mark)
   A. Who, where, when, what happened and how you felt
   B. Nothing
   C. Only the name
   D. Only the date

22. What should you do if a stranger promises cheap goods and asks for money first? (1 mark)
   A. Send money at once
   B. Be careful and ask an adult
   C. Give your address
   D. Trust them

23. Which word joins two ideas that contrast? (1 mark)
   A. and
   B. so
   C. because
   D. but

24. What does change mean in a shop? (1 mark)
   A. The weather
   B. The clothes
   C. Money given back after paying
   D. A journey

25. Which is a compound sentence? (1 mark)
   A. I bought a pen.
   B. I saved money, so I bought a pen.
   C. The red pen.
   D. A pen

26. Which is a domestic animal? (1 mark)
   A. Zebra
   B. Lion
   C. Goat
   D. Elephant

27. The ball is touching the top of the table. Which preposition fits? (1 mark)
   A. behind
   B. on
   C. outside
   D. under

28. Which is a good tip for reciting? (1 mark)
   A. Speak very fast
   B. Cover your face
   C. Look at the audience and speak clearly
   D. Look at the floor and mumble

29. Why record yourself reciting? (1 mark)
   A. To stop practising
   B. To listen back and improve
   C. To delete your voice
   D. To lose the poem

30. Which interjection shows disgust? (1 mark)
   A. Aha
   B. Hurray
   C. Bravo
   D. Yuck

31. What is community service? (1 mark)
   A. Helping the community without pay
   B. Sleeping
   C. Selling goods
   D. Playing only

32. What should a dialogue about leisure show? (1 mark)
   A. Unkindness
   B. Good values such as responsibility
   C. Rudeness
   D. Bad habits

33. Why should you ask permission before using someone's phone? (1 mark)
   A. Phones never break
   B. It belongs to them and needs care
   C. It is illegal to touch phones
   D. It is a game

34. What should you do first when a call is answered? (1 mark)
   A. Greet politely
   B. Hang up
   C. Ask for money
   D. Shout

35. Which sentence uses an adjective? (1 mark)
   A. The heavy computer is on the table.
   B. The computer is on.
   C. On the table.
   D. Computers work.

36. What is a product? (1 mark)
   A. A time
   B. A place
   C. A thing made or grown for sale
   D. A poem

37. What does turn taking mean? (1 mark)
   A. Speaking one at a time and waiting for your chance
   B. Speaking all at once
   C. Refusing to speak
   D. Speaking loudest

38. What are images in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Maps
   B. Words that make pictures in the mind
   C. Photographs
   D. Diagrams

39. What are non-verbal cues in a performance? (1 mark)
   A. Written words
   B. Music only
   C. Loud shouting
   D. Gestures and facial expressions

40. What is an instruction chart? (1 mark)
   A. A drawing of a house
   B. A story chart
   C. A list of animals
   D. A poster showing steps for a task

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Join the sentences with when: I counted my money. The bell rang. (2 marks)

42. State three rules for a debate. (3 marks)

43. Complete each sentence with a suitable verb: (a) We ______ our hands before eating. (b) Please ______ the door. (3 marks)

44. Give three qualities of a good leader mentioned in the model poem lead with honesty. (3 marks)

45. Explain how to take part in a class handwriting gallery walk. (4 marks)

46. Describe how a class can start a reading club. (4 marks)

47. Choose one proverb and explain its meaning. Then describe a real situation at school where it would apply. (5 marks)

48. Give three steps for telling a story fluently. (3 marks)

49. Write a short speech of four sentences about caring for a goat. Use at least two prepositions. (5 marks)

50. Give two examples of constructive leisure activities. (2 marks)

51. List three steps for explaining a proverb. (3 marks)

52. Give three money words and their meanings. (3 marks)

53. Write a four-line dialogue between two friends deciding what to do in their free time. Use two interjections. (4 marks)

54. Plan a reader's theatre for a short passage about rain. Say who the roles are, how to practise and how the audience gives feedback. (5 marks)

55. Give two features of a poem. (2 marks)

56. Copy this sentence correctly: the food is hot (2 marks)

57. Name three questions to ask yourself before telling a personal experience. (3 marks)

58. Give two adjectives to describe a mobile phone. (2 marks)

59. Name two prepositions used to show position. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — So you can find their meanings and learn them
   Underlining marks the words to study.

2. D — Writing that can be read easily
   Legible means easy to read.

3. A — A text that is spoken
   Oral means spoken.

4. A — Are you coming to school?
   It is a question.

5. D — Sitting where you can see and hear the speaker
   You can follow better when you see and hear clearly.

6. C — Who
   Who asks about people.

7. B — He touched the handle of the hot pot
   He moved closer and touched the handle, and the pot tipped.

8. D — In alphabetical order
   Dictionaries use alphabetical order.

9. C — Practise your lines with the right feeling
   Practice with expression helps fluency.

10. B — First
   First begins the sequence.

11. C — The classroom was a beehive.
   A metaphor says one thing is another.

12. C — Choose a comparison your listeners will understand
   Clear and kind comparisons work best.

13. D — A group that meets to share and discuss books
   A reading club shares books and reading.

14. C — It is fast and does not disturb others
   Silent reading is quiet and lets you think.

15. D — Work is easier when people share it
   It is a proverb about working together.

16. A — A girl called Neema
   Characters are the people or animals.

17. B — solves the problem or shows the lesson
   Endings resolve the story.

18. B — A stitch in time saves nine
   It is a short saying that gives advice.

19. B — A conjunction
   When joins two ideas by time.

20. C — Something that happened to you
   A personal experience is an event you lived.

21. A — Who, where, when, what happened and how you felt
   These details make the event clear.

22. B — Be careful and ask an adult
   Such offers may be tricks.

23. D — but
   But shows contrast.

24. C — Money given back after paying
   Change is the money you get back.

25. B — I saved money, so I bought a pen.
   It joins two sentences with so.

26. C — Goat
   Goats are kept by people.

27. B — on
   On shows contact with the top.

28. C — Look at the audience and speak clearly
   Eye contact and clarity help.

29. B — To listen back and improve
   Playback shows how to improve.

30. D — Yuck
   Yuck shows disgust.

31. A — Helping the community without pay
   Community service benefits others.

32. B — Good values such as responsibility
   Dialogues can teach values.

33. B — It belongs to them and needs care
   Respecting others' property is polite.

34. A — Greet politely
   A greeting begins the call.

35. A — The heavy computer is on the table.
   Heavy describes the computer.

36. C — A thing made or grown for sale
   A product is a thing for sale.

37. A — Speaking one at a time and waiting for your chance
   Turn taking is orderly speaking.

38. B — Words that make pictures in the mind
   Images are word pictures.

39. D — Gestures and facial expressions
   Non-verbal cues are actions without words.

40. D — A poster showing steps for a task
   It shows steps in order.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: When I counted my money, the bell rang.
   Working / marking points: One mark for using when and one mark for the comma.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen without interrupting, speak politely, give reasons, accept the result graciously, take turns.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: wash (or clean) and close (or shut)
   Working / marking points: One mark for each suitable verb and one mark for correct spelling.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fair, true, listens, shares the work, kind, strong (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Write your best sentence on a strip. Display it on the wall. Walk quietly, look at each strip, and leave a kind and helpful comment.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Collect books, choose a name and a librarian, agree on rules for borrowing, meet regularly to read and share books, and record who borrowed each book.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct points.

47. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any correct proverb with a sensible meaning and a matching situation, for example A stitch in time saves nine means fix small problems early, such as mending a small tear in a uniform before it grows.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the proverb, two marks for the meaning and two marks for a clear situation.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Know the story well, speak clearly, keep a steady pace, change your voice for characters, look at the audience, end with the lesson.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

49. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four clear sentences with two prepositions, for example Give the goat water beside the food. Build a shed behind the house. Do not put a heavy load on it. Call the veterinary doctor if it is sick.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence and one mark for correct prepositions.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: Reading, sports, drawing, singing, gardening, community service (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say it slowly, picture what it shows, decide the lesson, think of a real situation, explain in your own words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Trade: buying and selling. Profit: money gained. Customer: person who buys. Price: cost of something.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each word with its meaning.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four lines with speaker names, colons, a clear topic and two suitable interjections.
   Working / marking points: One mark for names and colons, one mark for suitable content, one mark for each interjection.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Roles such as narrator, farmer, child and rain. Read your part silently three times, mark stressed words, then read aloud with expression. The audience gives one good point and one improvement.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for suitable roles, two marks for practice steps and one mark for feedback.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Short lines, stanzas, rhyme, rhythm, images (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: The food is hot.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the capital letter and one mark for the full stop.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Who was there, what happened, where, when, why, how did I feel.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each question.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: small, black, thin, new, flat (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sensible adjective.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: on, in, under, behind, beside, between, in front of, outside (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
